items.text: Videos received by Iran International show a group of students in the Motekhasesin neighborhood of Kermanshah city on Saturday, 30 Aban, came to the streets and shouted "Sogand Sayadi." According to reports, government forces beat them.

Today, Sunday, a number of Social Security and cultural retirees gathered in front of the Social Security Organization building in Tehran. In addition to their labor demands, the retirees chanted protest slogans and held placards demanding the halt of death sentences and the release of imprisoned teachers.

It was reported that in less than 48 hours, the price of macaroni increased by 100%, Iran Khodro products up to one billion tomans, tires by 30%, dairy products by 15%, and transportation costs by 22%. Reports from Mazandaran, Rasht, Gilan, and Isfahan describe problems such as expensive bread, power outages, lack of gas, rising prices of soda and food items, and cuts in subsidies. A retiree from Isfahan said his 20 million toman salary after 30 years of work is insufficient and his ration card and subsidies have been cut.

According to videos received by Iran International, a group of students in the Motekhassesin neighborhood of Kermanshah city came to the streets on Saturday, 30 Aban, shouting "Sogand Sayadi." According to reports, government forces beat them.

The head of the Cancer Management Group at the Ministry of Health announced that about 142,000 new cancer cases are registered annually in Iran, with men constituting more than half of these cases. Beheshtian identified tobacco, unhealthy diet, and physical inactivity as risk factors and emphasized early screening if there is a family history.

Zelensky requested the United States to authorize the transfer of Patriot missile interceptors, the cost of which was previously paid by Ukraine's allies. This request was made after a Russian drone attack on a five-story residential building in the city of Dymer.

Narges Mohammadi, Nobel Peace Prize laureate, reacted to the transfer of Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran, two political prisoners sentenced to death in the Ekbatan case, to solitary confinement in Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj and called to prevent the execution of their death sentences. Mohammadi stated that the death sentences had previously been overturned by the criminal court, but Branch 15 of the Revolutionary Court, headed by Abolghasem Salavati, sentenced them to death again. She also said Armoon and Najaran were tried in closed courts without adherence to even the laws of the Islamic Republic.

European Union member countries opposed the approval of the final agreement of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31). The closing session of this conference began on Sunday in Antalya, Turkey, after hours of negotiations among country representatives. Due to disagreements among countries and prolonged negotiations, the conference lasted 44 hours longer than scheduled, breaking the record for the longest UN climate meeting.

The water of the Dirmendere River passing through the center of Rize in northeastern Turkey suddenly turned red, shocking residents. Local authorities identified a private tea factory as the source of pollution using a drone, which discharged untreated wastewater directly into the river. The factory has been fined and water samples have been sent to a laboratory for examination.

Juventus defeated Venezia 4-0 in the twelfth week of Italy's Serie A with four goals in the second half. Nic Voltemade, Ton Koopmeiners, Juan Cuadrado, and Randal Kolo Muani were the goal scorers for Juventus. Kolo Muani converted a penalty that he himself had won into a goal.
A video received by Iran International shows protesters in Shahroud writing the slogan "Long live the Shah" on the wall opposite the Industrial University.

According to information received by Iran International, a number of students were arrested during the gathering on Saturday, 30 Aban in Kermanshah, protesting the killing of Sogand Sayadi. During this gathering, slogans including "Death to the dictator" were chanted.

In continuation of the Social Security retirees' protests, today, Sunday, 1 Azar, a group of them gathered in front of the Social Security building in Rasht. The retirees demanded a salary increase in line with inflation and living costs, as well as attention to their medical and supplementary insurance issues. They also held placards and chanted slogans demanding the release of teachers and political prisoners.

Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran, two prisoners sentenced to death in the "Ekbatān Town" case and detainees of the 1401 nationwide protests, were transferred to solitary confinement in Qezelhesar Prison in Karaj. Their death sentences were confirmed by the Supreme Court. They were moved to Suite 35, Unit 3 of Qezelhesar Prison.

According to videos received by Iran International, a group of students in Kermanshah took to the streets on Saturday, 30 Aban, protesting against the principal of Rezvan High School where "Sogand Sayadi" studies. According to reports, government forces beat them.

Javad Nekounam, head coach of Tractor, said in a press conference before the match against Al Wasl UAE that his team must enter the field with high focus and full mental readiness. He emphasized that the game is tough and the smarter team has a better chance for the desired result. Nekounam also mentioned the difficulties in reaching this stage and said every match is like a final for the team.

The Israeli army confirmed that it has joint plans with the US for a scenario of attack and resumption of war with Iran, and estimates that the time for Donald Trump's decision on action against Iran is near.

On the first of Azar, reports emerged of power outages in Mashhad, Varamin, Gonbad Kavus, and Lorestan. People complained about problems caused by the outages such as dark classrooms, gas cuts, and lack of internet and water. Some reports attributed the power outages to the sale of Iran's energy resources to neighboring countries.
A video sent to Iran International shows a one-week water cut and water supply by tanker in the village of Kuhabad, Taybad County, in Razavi Khorasan Province.

Mohammad Jafar Asadi, former deputy inspector of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, said that religious rulings may change over different periods. He added that jurists may have differing views on a subject. Asadi also said he is not a jurist and that answering this question is up to the jurists.

Mohammad Sharghi, detained during the protests of Dey 1404 and a security staff member at Mehrabad Airport in Tehran, has been sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. He was sentenced for operational actions for hostile governments and membership in "oppositional" groups. His case is currently under review at Branch 9 of the Supreme Court.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International on Sunday, the first of Azar, showing the polluted air in Tehran and said: "We also have no electricity, water, or gas. This air is making us nauseous."

Fars News Agency reported the sentencing of Zahra Inchahdargahi, former head of the Gymnastics Federation, to two years of imprisonment and permanent dismissal from government services in a currency embezzlement case.

The murders of Parvaneh Eskandari and Dariush Forouhar on 22 November 1998 revealed state-organized killings. Shortly after, the bodies of Mohammad Mokhtari and Mohammad Pooyandeh were found with signs of strangulation. The Ministry of Intelligence admitted responsibility for 4 murders, but these killings have continued since the start of the Islamic Republic.

Milad Taqaddosi, deputy of treatment at Neyshabur University of Medical Sciences, announced that by noon on Sunday, 1 Azar, 72 people have been poisoned due to consumption of alcoholic beverages, and the number of victims has increased to 4. Mojtaba Mohebati, commander of Neyshabur police, reported the arrest of 12 suspects related to the production and distribution of toxic alcoholic drinks. Investigations to identify other individuals involved in this case continue.

Milad Farahani, former goalkeeper of several Premier League and First Division football teams in Iran, died this morning in a car accident on the Karaj to Rasht route. He played for teams including Paykan, Damash Gilan, Gol Gohar Sirjan, Saba Qom, Naft Tehran, Naft Masjed Soleyman, Shahr Khodro, Havadar, and Khoshe Talaei. His last football experience was with Mes Sungun Varzaghan.

The Iran Human Rights Organization in Norway confirmed on Saturday, 30 Aban, that Milad Armoon and Navid Najaran, two protesters of "Woman, Life, Freedom," are at imminent risk of execution. These two political prisoners were transferred to solitary confinement in Qezel Hesar prison. Iranian media reported on 3 Khordad that death sentences were issued for them, although they had previously been acquitted of the death penalty.
A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that the electricity in their area in Qods city was cut off without prior notice on Sunday, 1 Azar, and they have no electricity or gas.

Zahra Nosratpour, a citizen from Rasht, has been summoned to Lakan prison in the city to serve a prison sentence. She was previously sentenced by the judiciary to a total of four years, six months, and three days in prison, of which 31 months and 16 days are enforceable as the severest punishment against her.

Reports have emerged of Russian projectiles falling in Poland and violations of Finnish and Moldovan airspace. The NATO Secretary General, referring to escalating tensions on Europe's eastern borders, emphasized that this military alliance will defend Poland's territorial integrity.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations announced on Sunday, 1 Azar, that it received a report about an incident involving an oil tanker and military forces in the Sea of Oman. The organization urged vessels to review the latest maritime security information and remain alert to changes in the operational conditions of the area. The UK Maritime Trade Operations stated that relevant authorities have been informed of the incident and investigations are ongoing.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center reported that since 25 Aban, seven oil tankers have been attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, and the security threat level in this waterway remains "severe." Three oil tankers were targeted by unidentified projectiles on 29 and 30 Aban while exiting the Strait of Hormuz, with two tankers catching fire. The center also stated that attacks and harassment actions by the IRGC against commercial ships continue, and Iran's claim about oil tankers hitting naval mines has not been confirmed.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International reporting a 66% increase in hamburger prices over six months: "It has risen from 475,400 tomans in Esfand 1404 to 790,000 tomans in Mehr 1405."

Contrary to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, at least 1,642 female students from various cities in Iran were sent to operational areas in the south of the country as part of the so-called "Rahian-e Noor" tours, despite Iran's international commitments not to involve children in military activities.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported an incident between a tanker and military forces in the Sea of Oman. The organization did not provide further details and said investigations are ongoing. No information has been released about the ownership of the tanker or the identity of the military forces.
Amid the intensifying fuel crisis and rising transportation costs, truck drivers' strikes have expanded in various cities in Iran, and groups of Nissan and pickup drivers have also joined them.

President Trump spoke about the ongoing conflict with Iran and said he intends to resume attacks on Iran after the New Year if no agreement is reached. He said talks continue indirectly and described the Iranians as "professional tap dancers," adding that they keep talking.

Israeli media have reported that the US and Israel have drafted joint plans for a possible renewed attack on the Islamic Republic. At the same time, an attack on a civilian facility in Bahrain and its condemnation by Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar have increased concerns about escalating tensions.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced that if no agreement is reached with the Islamic Republic, he intends to resume military attacks on Iran after the start of the new Gregorian year. He said indirect talks with the Islamic Republic continue but criticized the negotiation process. Trump also warned that if Iranian vessels attempt to break the US naval blockade, all of them will go to the bottom of the sea.
A new wave of truck drivers' strikes in Iran has been reported. Protests and anti-government graffiti continue. This news was reported by Iran International.
A video received by Iran International shows the installation of a poster with the design of the Lion and Sun flag in support of the Abdanan protests on a wall in southern Tehran.

The tanker tracking institute, Tanker Trackers, denied claims of an Iranian tanker named "Khatshkan" moving towards the Sea of Oman and stated that such a tanker does not exist. These reports emerged while the US naval blockade has entered its 130th day and the Islamic Republic's oil exports face severe restrictions.

The death sentence of a prisoner accused of murder was carried out on Tuesday, 26 Aban, at the Central Prison of Karaj. Additionally, three death row convicts in Mazandaran province and a woman in a case in Tehran were released from the gallows due to the forgiveness of the victims' families.

Ali Kowsari, deputy of education at the Basij Mostazafan Organization, said that simultaneously with the 5th of Azar, the anniversary of the Basij's establishment, the "Janfadaian" training program will start in 110 locations across the country. He added that the Basij is planning to build field training bases near several historical sites including Persepolis, Arg-e Bam, Chogha Zanbil Ziggurat in Shush, and Ferdowsi's tomb, and the execution of some of these projects will begin in the coming days.

Planned power outages began on Sunday, the first of Azar, in various regions of Iran. Tavanir Company announced new restrictions on electricity supply for residential and commercial customers due to fuel shortages at power plants. The outages may last up to two hours every two days and in some areas up to two hours per day.

More than 100 service workers of Yasuj Municipality reported non-payment of three months of their salaries. Workers of the machinery unit of Travers Karaj company protested against wage, insurance problems, and lack of job security. Also, a group of Social Security retirees reported delays in the payment of their November pensions.

Mohammad Maljo, an economist and economic researcher, has been sentenced to one year of imprisonment by a judicial authority. His court sessions were held in early Tir and mid-Mehr 1405. The report prepared by the interrogators of the IRGC Intelligence Organization was the basis for issuing the one-year imprisonment sentence against him.

Liverpool football team defeated Manchester United 4-0 in the 11th week of the English Premier League at Anfield stadium. Lenny Yaro's red card in the eighth minute left United with 10 players from the start of the match. Mauricio Pochettino began his first match as Manchester United coach with a heavy defeat.
Yadollah Motaei, a citizen from Dehgolan imprisoned in Qorveh prison, was sentenced to 39 months and two days in prison by the judiciary of Dehgolan county.

The number of detainees in Darreh Shahr increased to 6. Including two other citizens named Mohammad Olad and Hamid Mirzaei, the number of detainees on Friday, 29 Aban in Darreh Shahr county reached six. Earlier, the arrest of four other citizens named Amir Garavand, Ali Vali, Aryan Imani, and Erfan Esmaeili was reported.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International on Sunday, the first of Azar, showing mazut burning at the Shazand power plant in Arak and severe air pollution.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said in the Cheshmandaz program that the truck drivers' strike in 1404 expanded to at least 150 cities, but censorship, repression, and security arrests prevented its continuation and expansion.

Two citizens were arrested by the IRGC intelligence forces due to activities in cyberspace. A video of their forced confessions has been released, but the conditions under which it was recorded are unclear.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, said that energy reform is the "most urgent and important issue" of the country both during peace and today, but gasoline "is not worth reforming at all" and should be the "last issue." He added that gasoline accounts for 9% and gas 73% of energy consumption in Iran, and solving the gas issue "can solve the people's and government's problems" and bring economic security and social resilience.

The human rights group Halvash reported on Sunday, 1 Azar, with a video that hundreds of heavy vehicles have been stuck in line over the past few days at the Rimdan border crossing in Sistan and Baluchestan province. Drivers reported disorder in queue management, lack of welfare facilities, and the risk of spoilage of fruit and vegetable shipments.

Nine months after Khamenei's removal, a senior researcher of the Resistance Front revealed Mossad's infiltration at the highest level of the Islamic Republic. According to him, Mossad, by capturing the regime's intelligence institutions, became the source of information for Iran's leaders about Israel and was able to shape their narrative in its favor.

According to the monthly report of Aban 1405 by the Statistics Department of the Human Rights Activists in Iran, at least 75 prisoners including one woman were executed in Iran. During this period, 31 death sentences including one for a woman were issued and seven death sentences were confirmed by the Supreme Court. Notable cases include the execution of several detainees from the December 1404 protests and the issuance of a death sentence against Amirhossein Mousavi, a political prisoner in Evin prison.

Alireza Hosseinali-zadeh, the police commander of Mashhad, announced that in an attack by two individuals on police officers on Emamat Boulevard in this city, three officers were superficially injured. The police shot both attackers and one of them died after being transferred to the hospital. This incident occurred on Sunday evening at the beginning of Emamat Boulevard in Mashhad.
A video received by Iran International shows protesters in Dehloran writing the slogan "Salute to Abdanan" on a public wall in support of the protesting people of Abdanan.

Officials from the medical universities of Nishapur and Shiraz reported that about 150 people were poisoned due to consuming counterfeit alcoholic beverages in Nishapur, Shiraz, and Marvdasht. So far, five people have died, one person has suffered brain death, and several poisoned individuals are hospitalized in intensive care units. In Nishapur, 120 people were poisoned and four have died, while in Shiraz and Marvdasht about 30 people were poisoned and one person has died.

The human rights website Harana reported that Mohammad Sharghi, a security staff member at Mehrabad Airport and detainee of the January protests, has been sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court.

A presenter on the Islamic Republic's state TV questioned Bahrain's independence during a live program on Channel 3, saying they would like to declare Bahrain as Iran's 32nd province. He mocked Bahrain's request for action against the Islamic Republic, saying Bahrain's bigger ally has come and could do nothing. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry had earlier condemned the Islamic Republic's air attack on a non-military industrial complex and called for UN Security Council action.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing pomegranate sellers' vans on Saveh road and said that municipality officers shut down their business and took their scales.
Milad Farahani, former goalkeeper of several Premier League and First Division football teams in Iran, died on Sunday morning due to a traffic accident on the road from Karaj to Rasht.
The football teams Foolad Khuzestan and Sepahan Isfahan drew 2-2 in the 13th week of the Iranian Premier League. This match was one of the most beautiful games of this season of Iranian football.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said Trump says if no agreement is reached, attacks will resume after the New Year. He added Trump's threat is serious but the attack could start earlier and unexpectedly. Veysi asked if this means the Islamic Republic is safe from a US attack for the next forty days.

A group of Iranians gathered in front of the federal building in Los Angeles and condemned the continued suppression of citizens in support of the Abdanan protests. This was reported by Niloufar Mansouri, a reporter for Iran International, along with her interview with participants in this gathering.

Trump predicted that if Democrats win the November 3 midterm elections, stock markets would crash and the Islamic Republic of Iran would become more aggressive in its attacks. He said Iran launched more drones and missiles last week than at any time in over a year, but all were shot down without causing damage. Trump also claimed that both Democrats and Iran fought to keep oil prices high, but since the election, oil prices have fallen sharply.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced on the evening of Sunday, 1 Azar, that the Islamic Republic has killed 81,000 protesters up to this date. He said that Iran has launched more drones and missiles in the past week than at any time in over a year, and all were intercepted and shot down. Trump also accused the Democrats and the Islamic Republic of trying to keep oil prices high and described the recent election as "very strange."

Farzad Talakesh, Secretary General of the Iran Poultry Federation, stated that the reasonable price for a tray of eggs for consumers is between 700,000 to 750,000 tomans and the price of chicken meat is about 400,000 to 430,000 tomans per kilogram. He also said that chicken meat consumption has decreased by more than 25 percent compared to the same period.
